claim: Orchestration architecture alone governs baseline scalability in multi-agent LLM systems: simpler architectures (Direct LLM calls) achieve the lowest latency and highest throughput, while more complex architectures (e.g., Concordia) incur significantly higher latency and lower throughput.
falsifier: Compare latency and throughput of different orchestration architectures under identical models and tasks; the claim predicts that Direct LLM calls will have lowest latency and highest throughput, while Concordia will have highest latency and lowest throughput.

exclusions: limited to the reported frameworks, models, and tasks; transfer beyond them is unestablished

title: Orchestration architecture–baseline scalability mechanism
